chapter: First bands and brass band practice
title: Reading music and the country brass band teacher
summary: Parker's band read music taught by professors; Jim Humphrey taught country bands in the parishes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah. What kind of music did you play? Huh? What kind of music did you play? The brass band.
What kind of music did you play?
Did you read or did you play by ear?

Oh, read. We had a professor. Uh huh. You understand your professor Hinger? Uh huh. Then I had a fellow up there and used to come home and teach. They called him, what is his name again? The name again. R.C.B.I. Creole for a trumpet player. He died. Yes. He used to teach down there. Old Jim Humphrey used to teach. You heard of Jim Humphrey?
Yes, I know his grandchildren and his son. Yeah, George.
Well, he taught all them bands down there.
This was down in the country?

Yes, indeed. He'd come down there. He'd come to us, maybe Sunday. He'd stay with us two days. Then he'd go to Dameron and stay two days. Then he'd go to Magnolia and stay two days, where the son of him would come from. He'd be taught all them bands. See, at that time they had bands. Magnolia, Point Lash, Derry, St. Sofa, Irontan, Bel-Air. Oakville, Judge and Bend. Oakville, George's Bend, all them places had a band, you see. And old hombre had all that voice. He didn't charge it for two bits of less. Two bits of less.
